messages:
rachel: hey team, first day and my PR shows GH Actions passing but Buildkite fails instantly on webhook/auth when opening against infra/helm-sandbox. Any quick triage?

 diego: welcome! paste the Buildkite error and say whether you're running the agent as a service on Windows, systemd on linux, or in k8s.

 rachel: running the agent as a Windows service on a company laptop. error in Buildkite UI: 
```
2026-03-30T15:34:12Z ERROR webhook: 403 Forbidden - installation not found for org
```

 kim: that 403 is the GitHub App not installed/authorized for the org or repo. If your laptop is using an old agent token and the webhook can't create a check run for the PR, you'll see both a webhook 403 and agent 401s.

 rachel: agent logs also show: 
```
ERR: buildkite-agent: failed to register: 401 Unauthorized - token invalid or revoked
```

 diego: two paths: 1) ensure the GH App is installed for the org/repo (GitHub -> Org settings -> Installed GitHub Apps -> Redwood CI -> Configure -> grant access). 2) regenerate an agent token and update the Windows service. For Windows the token lives in `C:\ProgramData\buildkite-agent\buildkite-agent.cfg`.

 rachel: i don't have org admin to change the app. also i got my agent token from an onboarding DM yesterday, could that be stale?

 kim: yes infra rotates join tokens. DM tokens are short-lived. Ask infra to add the repo or create a scoped team token. I'll request the app install. Meanwhile update your local token: run PowerShell as admin and `Stop-Service buildkite-agent; (Get-Content 'C:\ProgramData\buildkite-agent\buildkite-agent.cfg') -replace 'token=".*"', 'token="<NEW_TOKEN>"' | Set-Content 'C:\ProgramData\buildkite-agent\buildkite-agent.cfg'; Start-Service buildkite-agent`.

 infra-bot: Request filed: add 'infra/helm-sandbox' to Redwood CI installation by @kim. Approvers: @diego, @mel.

 buildkite-bot: Buildkite build #501 failed: see https://buildkite.com/redwood/infra/501/jobs/2

 diego: approved, adding repo now. Also note: on Windows if your agent was started under an account without access to `C:\ProgramData` changes may not apply. Make sure the service runs as 'LocalSystem' or an account with file perms.

 rachel: infra added the repo. updated token and restarted service. Re-triggering build...

 buildkite-bot: Buildkite build #502 started: https://buildkite.com/redwood/infra/502

 rachel: build picked up but failing on image pull: 
```
failed to pull image "gcr.io/redwood-ci/helm-base:stable": 403 Forbidden - access denied
```

 kim: if you're on a laptop using Docker Desktop, ensure `gcloud auth configure-docker` has been run with the CI service account, or use `docker-credential-gcr` configured. For laptops we usually mount short-lived creds in `~/.docker/config.json`. If you reused a machine, you might be missing the CI SA key.

 diego: for k8s/helm folks there's also an edge: if you deployed buildkite agents with our Helm chart, the chart's values.yaml contains the token secret and imagePullSecret name. If infra rotated tokens, the Helm release needs `--set agent.token=<new-token>` or secret update + `helm upgrade` then `kubectl rollout restart` for the agent deployment.

 rachel: i'm on laptop, ran `gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file C:\ci-creds\gcr-key.json` after infra pushed the key via SSM. docker pull works now. re-run pipeline.

 buildkite-bot: Buildkite build #502 succeeded.

 rachel: tests passed! thanks everyone. Two follow-ups: 1) can we add a one-liner in onboarding for Windows agent path + service restart? 2) who to ping for token rotations that affect Helm values or k8s secrets?

 kim: yes on both. Please open a small PR to onboarding docs with Windows steps (`C:\ProgramData\...` note + service restart) and tag it 'windows-agent'. For rotations ping #eng-infra and @infra-bot; if you use Helm chart also ping @platform so we can update CI Helm values in the chart repo.

 rachel: will do. appreciate the help! :wave:
